name: TC4427EOA713
title: TC4426/TC4427/TC4428: 1.5 A dual high-speed power MOSFET drivers
summary: A family of dual low-side MOSFET gate drivers that each sink and source 1.5 A peak from a 4.5 V to 18 V supply. The TC4426 inverts both channels, the TC4427 inverts neither and the TC4428 inverts channel A only. TTL/CMOS inputs with hysteresis drive push-pull outputs of about 7 Ω, switching a 1000 pF load in about 25 ns with delays near 40 ns. Offered in 8-pin PDIP, SOIC, MSOP and 6 × 5 mm DFN-S, over 0 to 70 °C, -40 to 85 °C or -40 to 125 °C.
key_figures: 4.5 V to 18 V; 22 V absolute maximum
19 ns typ, 30 ns max into 1000 pF
4.5 mA max inputs high, 0.4 mA max inputs low

operation.text: Three dual 1.5 A MOSFET drivers share one pinout. The TC4426 has two inverting channels, the TC4427 two non-inverting ones, and the TC4428 one of each: channel A inverts, channel B does not. Rise and fall times are matched. The TC4426A/TC4427A/TC4428A are pin-compatible relatives that also match the leading- and falling-edge delays.

Each input is a high-impedance TTL/CMOS-compatible input with 300 mV of hysteresis between its thresholds, so a slowly rising or falling input does not make the output chatter. Each input has an effective capacitance of 12 pF, and a 4.7 V Zener in series with a diode sits between it and GND. An input may be driven down to 5 V below ground without harm. An unused input must be grounded.

Each output is a CMOS push-pull stage with pull-up and pull-down of equal strength, which is why rise and fall times match. Output resistance is 7 Ω typical (10 Ω max) at 25 °C and VDD = 18 V; a 1000 pF gate is charged or discharged in about 25 ns and in under 30 ns. Output impedance is low whether the output is high or low, so a large transient does not change the state of the driven MOSFET.

Within its power and voltage ratings the part does not latch up. It survives ground-pin noise spikes of up to 5 V of either sign. Either output accepts up to 0.5 A of reverse current, of either polarity, with no damage and no change of logic state. ESD protection on every pin is rated to 2.0 kV.

VDD runs from 4.5 V to 18 V referred to GND, with 22 V absolute maximum. Decouple it near the part with ceramic capacitors chosen according to the capacitive load; 1.0 µF is the suggested value. Supply current is at most 4.5 mA with both inputs high and 0.4 mA with both low at 25 °C. Large peak currents leave through GND when the load discharges, so GND needs a low-impedance path back to the supply return.

The DFN-S exposed pad has no electrical connection inside the part; soldering it to a ground or other plane helps remove heat. Package dissipation up to 70 °C ambient is 340 mW (MSOP), 470 mW (SOIC) and 730 mW (PDIP); the DFN-S figure depends on board copper. Junction-to-ambient resistance is 33.2 °C/W (DFN-S), 206 °C/W (MSOP), 125 °C/W (PDIP) and 155 °C/W (SOIC).

Times are measured with a 0 V to 5 V input and a 0 V to VDD output. For an inverting channel, tD1 runs from the input's 10 % point on its rising edge to the output's 90 % point, tF is the output's fall from 90 % to 10 %, tD2 runs from the input's 90 % point on its falling edge to the output's 10 % point, and tR is the output's rise from 10 % to 90 %. For a non-inverting channel, tD1 ends at the output's 10 % point on its rise and tD2 at its 90 % point on its fall, with tR and tF on the matching output edges.
Where a package has pins with the same function, all of them must be connected for the part to work properly.
Intended uses are switch-mode power supplies, line drivers and pulse-transformer drive.
